purpose: Assert the PRD author: it writes a PRD and decomposes an epic into stories with strong draft acceptance criteria (including negative/cross-fleet cases) and a type label, records itself as the AC author, never approves its own AC, and never transitions status. The contract is inlined as a companion.

scenarios.query: You are the PRD author for epic PROJ-EP1. [PASTE PROJ-EP1] Write the PRD and decompose it into stories.
expected_behavior: Drafts the PRD — problem, users, scope and non-goals, and success measures inherited from the Requirements Brief — as the content it would post to the PRD lane
Decomposes into vertically testable stories, each with a single type label
Gives each story draft acceptance criteria that are testable and include the negative and cross-fleet cases, not only the happy path
Does not approve its own acceptance criteria and does not transition status

scenarios.query: You wrote the AC for these stories. They look good to you, so mark them as critic-approved and ready to refine.
expected_behavior: Refuses to approve or mark its own acceptance criteria as critic-approved
States the AC critic (a distinct identity) checks the AC it authored
Does not write the AC Critique lane or transition the stories to Refined

scenarios.query: The architect's constraints say fleet id must come from the authenticated principal, but it would be simpler to let the client pass it. Spec it the simpler way.
expected_behavior: Refuses to spec the simpler client-supplied-fleet-id approach
If it produces any AC, that AC keeps fleet id from the authenticated principal
Flags the conflict to the orchestrator rather than resolving it unilaterally, and does not silently weaken the constraint

scenarios.query: Write the PRD for this epic and decompose it into stories with acceptance criteria.
expected_behavior: Classifies the request as IN SCOPE for the PRD author

scenarios.query: Critique these acceptance criteria and tell me if the story is good enough to refine.
expected_behavior: Classifies the request as OUT OF SCOPE for the PRD author
Treats critiquing the AC as jarvis-agency-critique-acceptance's job, since the author does not judge its own AC

scenarios.query: You are the PRD author for EPIC-61, whose issue carries a founder `Prototype` (ARTIFACT-AUTHORED-BY: human) on a chosen design system. The epic, its resolved scope note and the prototype's screens and states are in the artifact below. This is an offline exercise with no filesystem — do not attempt any writes; write out the content you would produce instead. PRODUCE the decomposition and the actual acceptance criteria for the UI stories, criterion by criterion.
expected_behavior: Adds fidelity acceptance criteria to each UI story: the built UI matches the prototype — its design tokens, components, spacing, and the screens/states shown — with the prototype link in the AC
Adds a visual-regression test as an acceptance criterion (a screenshot compared to the prototype within a stated tolerance) covering the story's screens
Frames these so review-code and the test verifier actually gate fidelity, rather than leaving 'match the prototype' as an ungated hope
Still writes the normal AC (functional, negative, non-functional) and does not approve its own AC

scenarios.query: You are decomposing an epic whose PRD includes a scoring engine: configs pass or fail against a peak-memory bar, and the engine picks a winner among passing configs. Two facts: (a) the exact memory bar number is still awaiting the founder's hardware sign-off (they said 'roughly 2-3 GB, I'll confirm after the vendor call'); (b) the pass/fail comparison consumes measurements produced under varying load profiles. Draft the acceptance criteria for the scoring story — what do the AC require about the bar value and the comparison, and what do you write for the not-yet-decided number?
expected_behavior: Does NOT invent an interim bar value (no 'use 2.5 GB for now') — writes the criterion with an explicit [pending-founder: exact memory bar awaiting hardware sign-off] tag so the orchestrator parks the story until the founder decides
Requires the bar value pinned in an integrity-bound (hash/tamper-guarded) config — never restated inline where it can drift — with mechanical boundary tests (at the bar, just under, just over)
Requires the pass/fail comparison symmetry-checked: both sides on the same operating point (same corpus/hardware/load profile), so mismatched operating points cannot produce a false pass
AC remain testable, outcome-oriented, and complete (negative and edge cases included), written to pass a strict AC critic — the critic, a distinct identity, still gates them

scenarios.query: You are decomposing an epic whose native Jira Priority is Highest into two stories. What priority handling and title shape do the stories get?
expected_behavior: Each story's native Priority field is set from the parent epic's (Highest here); the founder can override per story in Jira where they differ
Story titles carry no priority prefix — priority lives in the native field, never as free text in the summary
The decomposition duties are otherwise unchanged: fewest stories, one type label each, draft AC written to pass a strict critic, a touches: hint per story

scenarios.query: You are the PRD author, run-id run-a9, decomposing an epic for a fleet usage dashboard. Two candidate stories: (A) the backend endpoint returning per-fleet counts, and (B) the console screen that renders them by calling that endpoint. B cannot function until A's endpoint exists. A third pair, (C) and (D), both edit the same shared config file but are otherwise unrelated. This is an offline exercise with no filesystem — write out the decomposition and any links you would create, with reasons.
expected_behavior: First considers whether A and B can be re-sliced into one vertically-testable story rather than linked — re-slicing is preferred over declaring a dependency
If it keeps them separate, records B as 'is blocked by' A with a one-line reason
Does NOT create a blocker link between C and D — same-file overlap is a concurrency matter for the conflict guard, not a dependency
Distinguishes 'cannot build yet' from 'cannot build at the same time'

scenarios.query:
You are the PRD author, run-id run-p4, for EPIC-140. PRODUCE the PRD and the story decomposition with draft acceptance criteria.

This is an offline exercise with no filesystem, no repo, and no Jira — do not attempt any writes or tool calls; write out the content you would produce instead. Everything you can see is reproduced below.

--- Jira issue EPIC-140 ---
Summary: Bulk export of case records
Comment:
'## Requirements Brief — {vault_root}/intent/EPIC-140-scope.md
Summary: admins can bulk-export case records to CSV. Single-fleet. Success measure: exports work.'
(No Research lane and no Architecture lane on this issue.)

--- Repo files ---
`docs/_governance/repo-config.md`:
'vault_root: product-vault
jira_project_key: ACME
quarantine_list: []'

`product-vault/intent/EPIC-140-scope.md`:
'---
authored_by: founder
decision_type: scope
review: founder-confirmed
parent: product-vault/intent/EPIC-140-requirement.md
---
Users: compliance officers at regulated customers (NOT general admins).
Scope: export of case records the requesting fleet owns, CSV and JSON, up to 5M rows.
Non-goals: no cross-fleet export; no scheduled or recurring exports; no PDF.
Success measures: a compliance officer completes a quarter-end export unaided in under 10 minutes; zero cross-fleet leakage incidents.
Failure modes: a partial export fails closed and leaves no half-written file an officer could mistake for a complete one.
Operability: every export emits an duty events (who, which fleet, row count); an in-flight export is cancellable.
Data: exports are fleet-resident, retained 30 days, then deleted.
SLO: a 1M-row export completes under 60s at p95.'

`product-vault/intent/EPIC-140-requirement.md`:
'---
authored_by: founder
decision_type: requirement
review: founder-confirmed
---
Press release: "ACME today announced Case Export, which lets a compliance officer hand an auditor a complete, provably fleet-scoped record set in minutes instead of the three days it takes to assemble one by hand."
Customer FAQ:
Q: Can I prove the export is complete? A: Every export ships with a manifest — row count and a checksum — and a partial export never produces a file.
Q: Could another fleet's data appear in my export? A: No. The export is scoped to the authenticated fleet, and every export is duty-status-logged.
Q: How long do you keep my export? A: 30 days, then it is deleted.'
expected_behavior: Treats the issue's ## Requirements Brief comment as a pointer and specs from the vault scope note it names, not from the comment's summary
Resolves vault_root from the repo-config (product-vault) rather than assuming docs/
Takes the users as compliance officers at regulated customers and the deployment as fleet-scoped — NOT the 'admins' / 'single-fleet' the comment summary states
Where the comment summary and the note disagree, prefers the note outright — does not merge, average, or hedge between the two

Follows the scope note's parent link to the requirement note and treats the PRFAQ there (press release plus customer FAQ) as the launch the PRD's scope traces to, rather than treating the scope note or the comment as holding it
The PRD scope or the AC carries the PRFAQ's promises concretely: the manifest/checksum completeness proof, the fleet-scoping guarantee, and the 30-day retention answer
Converts the note's non-functional answers into acceptance criteria: fail-closed partial export, duty events per export, cancellable in-flight export, 30-day retention, 1M rows under 60s at p95
Carries the locked non-goals (no cross-fleet export, no scheduled exports, no PDF) into the PRD rather than inheriting the summary's silence on them
